newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland may cancel anti-tank missile tender.
newsitem.headline: Poland may cancel anti-tank missile tender.

text.p: Poland may cancel a tender for anti-tank missiles worth $500 million which was won by Israeli firm Elbit, PAP news agency quoted a deputy industry minister as saying on Friday.
PAP news agency quoted Roman Czerwinski as telling a joint defence and industry parliamentary committee that Elbit was slow with deliveries and Poland currently had better offers from other firms.
"(We might cancel the tender) because the firm which won it is late with delivering the product and Poland now has more attractive offers from other firms," Czerwinski said.
The tender, closed earlier this year, was to supply Poland with a new Rafael missile. Details of the agreement with Elbit were not disclosed and officials were not immediately available for comment.
The missiles were to be installed on 150 Huzar combat helicopters, which the armed forces want to buy from the domestic PZL Swidnik firm.

In September the government's defence committee tentatively agreed to conclude the deal but military experts were to further examine the missile during a November visit to Israel before a final decision was taken.

At the tender the defence ministry rejected an offer of remotely-piloted Hellfire missiles from the U.S. Rockwell arms manufacturer, saying it was late for the deadline, as well as one for France's Aerospatiale's Hot-2 missile.

U.S. government officials pressed Polish authorities to let Rockwell join the tender and newspapers quoted analysts as saying that buying the missile from the United States would be advantageous, considering Poland's plans to join NATO. -- Jan Strupczewski +48 22 653 9700
